section_title: How do we stand together when believers disagree?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.

2 I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord. 3 Yes, and I ask you, my true yokefellow, to help these women who have contended at my side for the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Life.

context_lines: After describing the coming Savior and the transformation of His people, Paul tells these dearly loved believers to stand firm in the Lord. Calling them his joy and crown expresses how deeply their life in Christ matters to him.
He then appeals to Euodia and Syntyche to agree in the Lord. Their disagreement is real, but its subject is not given. Paul speaks to both women and asks a trusted companion to help them.

He also remembers their work beside him for the gospel, alongside Clement and his other coworkers. The appeal seeks reconciliation among valued fellow workers. It does not erase their service or turn their dispute into their whole identity.

The companion’s identity is uncertain. The [BSB footnote](https://biblehub.com/bsb/philippians/4.htm) allows the possibility of the name Syzygus. The text does not tell us that this helper was the pastor, nor does it identify Clement as the later bishop of Rome.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand this as a call to reconciliation and practical help within the church. [Wesley’s notes on verses 1–3](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-philippians/) emphasize Paul’s tender personal appeal; the [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/philippians/4) connect it with his earlier call to humility in Philippians 2:2–4. Their shared emphasis is on standing together in the Lord, without enough information to reconstruct the disagreement.
god_plan_lines: Jesus prays in [John 17:20–26](https://biblehub.com/bsb/john/17.htm) for those who will believe through His disciples’ message. He connects their unity with the world knowing that the Father sent Him, and He desires that they be with Him. Reconciliation serves that wider purpose of a people whose life together bears witness to Him.

The mention of the Book of Life also reaches beyond the present dispute. [Revelation 21:22–27](https://biblehub.com/bsb/revelation/21.htm) describes the final city lit by God’s glory and the Lamb, entered by those named in the Lamb’s Book of Life. Paul addresses these coworkers in light of their belonging to God’s people, not merely the tension between them.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
